# zgtsvx

> Uses the LU factorization to compute the solution to a complex system of.

<section class="intro">

linear equations A_X = B, A^T_X = B, or A^H_X = B, where A is a
tridiagonal matrix of order N and X and B are N-by-NRHS matrices.

Error bounds on the solution and a condition estimate are also provided.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zgtsvx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zgtsvx';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zgtsvx(
    order,
    fact, trans,
    N, nrhs,
    DL, strideDL,
    d, strideD,
    DU, strideDU,
    DLF, strideDLF,
    DF, strideDF,
    DUF, strideDUF,
    DU2, strideDU2,
    IPIV, strideIPIV,
    B, LDB,
    X, LDX,
    rcond,
    FERR, strideFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR,
    WORK,
    RWORK
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `fact` | `("not-factored"\|"factored")` | in |  | one of `'factored'`, `'not-factored'` | 'not-factored' or 'factored' |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | in |  | one of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'` | 'no-transpose', 'transpose', or 'conjugate-transpose' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix A |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | number of right hand sides |
| `DL` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | sub-diagonal of A (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDL` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DL (in complex elements) |
| `d` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N` |  | diagonal of A (length N) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for d (in complex elements) |
| `DU` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | super-diagonal of A (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDU` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DU (in complex elements) |
| `DLF` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N - 1` |  | factored sub-diagonal (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDLF` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DLF (in complex elements) |
| `DF` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N` |  | factored diagonal (length N) |
| ↳ `strideDF` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DF (in complex elements) |
| `DUF` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N - 1` |  | factored super-diagonal (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDUF` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DUF (in complex elements) |
| `DU2` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N - 2` |  | second superdiagonal fill-in (length N-2) |
| ↳ `strideDU2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DU2 (in complex elements) |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array` | in/out | `N` |  | pivot indices (length N) |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for IPIV |
| `B` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | right hand side matrix |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of B (in complex elements) |
| `X` | `Complex128Array` | out | `N × nrhs` |  | solution matrix (output) |
| ↳ `LDX` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDX ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDX ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of X (in complex elements) |
| `rcond` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | single-element array for reciprocal condition number |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | forward error bounds (output) |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for FERR |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | backward error bounds (output) |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for BERR |
| `WORK` | `(Complex128Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 2 * N` |  | workspace array |
| `RWORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ N` |  | real workspace array |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `fact`: Specifies whether or not the factored form of A has been supplied on entry.

  -   `= 'F'`: `DLF`, `DF`, `DUF`, `DU2`, and `IPIV` contain the factored form of A; `DL`, D, `DU`, `DLF`, `DF`, `DUF`, `DU2` and `IPIV` will not be modified.
  -   `= 'N'`: The matrix will be copied to `DLF`, `DF`, and `DUF` and factored.
- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations:

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$     (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose)
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `DL`: The (n-1) subdiagonal elements of A.
- `d`: The n diagonal elements of A.
- `DU`: The (n-1) superdiagonal elements of A.
- `DLF`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `DLF` is an input argument and on entry contains the (n-1) multipliers that define the matrix L from the LU factorization of A as computed by ZGTTRF.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `DLF` is an output argument and on exit contains the (n-1) multipliers that define the matrix L from the LU factorization of A.
- `DF`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `DF` is an input argument and on entry contains the n diagonal elements of the upper triangular matrix U from the LU factorization of A.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `DF` is an output argument and on exit contains the n diagonal elements of the upper triangular matrix U from the LU factorization of A.
- `DUF`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `DUF` is an input argument and on entry contains the (n-1) elements of the first superdiagonal of U.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `DUF` is an output argument and on exit contains the (n-1) elements of the first superdiagonal of U.
- `DU2`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `DU2` is an input argument and on entry contains the (n-2) elements of the second superdiagonal of U.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `DU2` is an output argument and on exit contains the (n-2) elements of the second superdiagonal of U.
- `IPIV`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `IPIV` is an input argument and on entry contains the pivot indices from the LU factorization of A as computed by ZGTTRF.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `IPIV` is an output argument and on exit contains the pivot indices from the LU factorization of A; row i of the matrix was interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`. `IPIV(i)` will always be either i or i+1; `IPIV(i) = i` indicates a row interchange was not required.
- `B`: The N-by-`NRHS` right hand side matrix B.
- `X`: If `INFO = 0` or $\mathrm{INFO} = N+1$, the N-by-`NRHS` solution matrix X.
- `rcond`: The estimate of the reciprocal condition number of the matrix A. If `RCOND` is less than the machine precision (in particular, if `RCOND = 0`), the matrix is singular to working precision. This condition is indicated by a return code of $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for `RCOND`, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "factored", "not-factored"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` twenty-third argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` twenty-third argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` twenty-fifth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` twenty-fifth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zgtsvx.ndarray(
    fact, trans,
    N, nrhs,
    DL, strideDL, offsetDL,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    DU, strideDU, offsetDU,
    DLF, strideDLF, offsetDLF,
    DF, strideDF, offsetDF,
    DUF, strideDUF, offsetDUF,
    DU2, strideDU2, offsetDU2,
    IPIV, strideIPIV, offsetIPIV,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    X, strideX1, strideX2, offsetX,
    rcond,
    FERR, strideFERR, offsetFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR, offsetBERR,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    RWORK, strideRWork, offsetRWork
) → info: integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fact` | `("not-factored"\|"factored")` | in |  | one of `'factored'`, `'not-factored'` | 'not-factored' or 'factored' |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | in |  | one of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'` | 'no-transpose', 'transpose', or 'conjugate-transpose' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix A |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | number of right hand sides |
| `DL` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | sub-diagonal of A (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDL` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DL (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetDL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for DL (in complex elements) |
| `d` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N` |  | diagonal of A (length N) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for d (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for d (in complex elements) |
| `DU` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | super-diagonal of A (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDU` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DU (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetDU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for DU (in complex elements) |
| `DLF` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N - 1` |  | factored sub-diagonal (length N-1), input if fact='factored', output if fact='not-factored' |
| ↳ `strideDLF` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DLF (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetDLF` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for DLF (in complex elements) |
| `DF` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N` |  | factored diagonal (length N), input if fact='factored', output if fact='not-factored' |
| ↳ `strideDF` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DF (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetDF` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for DF (in complex elements) |
| `DUF` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N - 1` |  | factored super-diagonal (length N-1), input if fact='factored', output if fact='not-factored' |
| ↳ `strideDUF` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DUF (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetDUF` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for DUF (in complex elements) |
| `DU2` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N - 2` |  | second superdiagonal fill-in (length N-2), input if fact='factored', output if fact='not-factored' |
| ↳ `strideDU2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DU2 (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetDU2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for DU2 (in complex elements) |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array` | in/out | `N` |  | pivot indices (length N), 0-based |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for IPIV |
| ↳ `offsetIPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for IPIV |
| `B` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | right hand side matrix (N x NRHS) |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of B (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of B (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for B (in complex elements) |
| `X` | `Complex128Array` | out | `N × nrhs` |  | solution matrix (N x NRHS), output |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of X (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of X (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for X (in complex elements) |
| `rcond` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output: rcond[0] is the reciprocal condition number |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | output: forward error bound for each RHS (length nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for FERR |
| ↳ `offsetFERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for FERR |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | output: backward error for each RHS (length nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for BERR |
| ↳ `offsetBERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for BERR |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array` | out | `≥ 2 * N` |  | workspace of length at least 2*N complex elements |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for WORK (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for WORK (in complex elements) |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ N` |  | real workspace of length at least N |
| ↳ `strideRWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for RWORK |
| ↳ `offsetRWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for RWORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `fact`: Specifies whether or not the factored form of A has been supplied on entry.

  -   `= 'F'`: `DLF`, `DF`, `DUF`, `DU2`, and `IPIV` contain the factored form of A; `DL`, D, `DU`, `DLF`, `DF`, `DUF`, `DU2` and `IPIV` will not be modified.
  -   `= 'N'`: The matrix will be copied to `DLF`, `DF`, and `DUF` and factored.
- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations:

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$     (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose)
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `DL`: The (n-1) subdiagonal elements of A.
- `d`: The n diagonal elements of A.
- `DU`: The (n-1) superdiagonal elements of A.
- `DLF`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `DLF` is an input argument and on entry contains the (n-1) multipliers that define the matrix L from the LU factorization of A as computed by ZGTTRF.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `DLF` is an output argument and on exit contains the (n-1) multipliers that define the matrix L from the LU factorization of A.
- `DF`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `DF` is an input argument and on entry contains the n diagonal elements of the upper triangular matrix U from the LU factorization of A.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `DF` is an output argument and on exit contains the n diagonal elements of the upper triangular matrix U from the LU factorization of A.
- `DUF`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `DUF` is an input argument and on entry contains the (n-1) elements of the first superdiagonal of U.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `DUF` is an output argument and on exit contains the (n-1) elements of the first superdiagonal of U.
- `DU2`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `DU2` is an input argument and on entry contains the (n-2) elements of the second superdiagonal of U.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `DU2` is an output argument and on exit contains the (n-2) elements of the second superdiagonal of U.
- `IPIV`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `IPIV` is an input argument and on entry contains the pivot indices from the LU factorization of A as computed by ZGTTRF.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `IPIV` is an output argument and on exit contains the pivot indices from the LU factorization of A; row i of the matrix was interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`. `IPIV(i)` will always be either i or i+1; `IPIV(i) = i` indicates a row interchange was not required.
- `B`: The N-by-`NRHS` right hand side matrix B.
- `X`: If `INFO = 0` or $\mathrm{INFO} = N+1$, the N-by-`NRHS` solution matrix X.
- `rcond`: The estimate of the reciprocal condition number of the matrix A. If `RCOND` is less than the machine precision (in particular, if `RCOND = 0`), the matrix is singular to working precision. This condition is indicated by a return code of $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for `RCOND`, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful, >0 if singular, N+1 if ill-conditioned

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "factored", "not-factored"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, and i is \<= N:  U(i,i) is exactly zero.  The factorization has not been completed unless $i = N$, but the factor U is exactly singular, so the solution and error bounds could not be computed. `RCOND = 0` is returned. = N+1: U is nonsingular, but `RCOND` is less than machine precision, meaning that the matrix is singular to working precision.  Nevertheless, the solution and error bounds are computed because there are a number of situations where the computed solution can be more accurate than the value of `RCOND` would suggest.

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import zgtsvx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zgtsvx';

// Solve A*x = b for a 3x3 complex tridiagonal system:
const dl = new Complex128Array( new Float64Array( [1, 0.5, 2, -1] ) );
const d = new Complex128Array( new Float64Array( [4, 1, 5, 0, 3, -0.5] ) );
const du = new Complex128Array( new Float64Array( [-1, 0.5, 1, 1] ) );
const dlf = new Complex128Array( 2 );
const df = new Complex128Array( 3 );
const duf = new Complex128Array( 2 );
const du2 = new Complex128Array( 1 );
const ipiv = new Int32Array( 3 );

// b = A * [1; 1; 1]
const b = new Complex128Array( new Float64Array( [3, 1.5, 8, 0.5, 5, -1.5] ) );
const x = new Complex128Array( 3 );
const rcond = new Float64Array( 1 );
const ferr = new Float64Array( 1 );
const berr = new Float64Array( 1 );
const work = new Complex128Array( 6 );
const rwork = new Float64Array( 3 );

const info = zgtsvx.ndarray( 'not-factored', 'no-transpose', 3, 1, dl, 1, 0, d, 1, 0, du, 1, 0, dlf, 1, 0, df, 1, 0, duf, 1, 0, du2, 1, 0, ipiv, 1, 0, b, 1, 3, 0, x, 1, 3, 0, rcond, ferr, 1, 0, berr, 1, 0, work, 1, 0, rwork, 1, 0 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'rcond:', rcond[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZGTSVX`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZGTSVX uses the LU factorization to compute the solution to a complex system of linear equations $A \, X = B$, $A^T \, X = B$, or $A^H \, X = B$, where A is a tridiagonal matrix of order N and X and B are N-by-`NRHS` matrices.

Error bounds on the solution and a condition estimate are also provided.

</section>
